To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the heifer development system of grazing corn residue or winter range did not affect pregnancy or reproductive performance.
heifer development system did affect (P < 0.01) prebreeding ADGs, but did not (P > 0.05) affect reproductive performance.
the heifer development system did affect (P < 0.01) ADG before breeding but did not affect ( P = 0.77) pregnancy rate.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of heifers for breeding, which is a critical step in a cow-calf system, and the effects of heifers development system (winter range or corn residue) on growth and pregnancy.
evaluating the use of corn residue as a forage resource in beef cattle operations.
the effect of heifer development systems on growth and reproductive performance.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
heifers can be developed using CR or WR and have similar reproductive performance and cost of development.
heifer development systems of corn residue or winter grazing did not affect pregnancy rates, calf performance, or development cost.

heifer development systems did not affect (1) pregnancy rate, (2) calf birth date, (3) calf birth BW, (4) cow BW, (5) calf weaning BW and 205-d adjusted calf BW, (6) dystocia, or (7) second season pregnancy rates.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have not been able to find a difference between corn residue and native range as a postweaning development system for heifers.
heifer development systems utilizing corn residues or winter range can be used interchangeably with no negative effects on reproductive performance.
heifer development systems that utilize corn residues as the forage source can be as effective as grazing winter range for developing heifers to first calving.
The main takeaway from our work is that
heifer development using CR is a viable option for beef producers.
heifer development systems using corn residue or winter range post-weaning can be used to develop heifers for breeding and calving without affecting performance or pregnancy rates.
we need to develop more efficient systems for developing replacement heifers.
